title: Scalar-twisted coset coproduct induction for scheme actions
statement:
Let $e\subseteq K$ be fields, let $G$ be a finite group, let $\pi:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$ be a homomorphism, and let $\Gamma\leq G$. Let $p:W\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be a scheme with a left $\Gamma$-action $d$ satisfying
$$p\circ d_\gamma=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi(\gamma)^{-1})\circ p.$$
Let $B$ be an $e$-scheme and let $q:W\to B$ be a $\Gamma$-invariant $e$-morphism. For any choice of representatives $s:G/\Gamma\to G$ of left cosets with $s(\Gamma)=1$, there exist a $K$-scheme $Y$, maps $t_g:W\to Y$ for all $g\in G$, a left $G$-action $a$ on $Y$, and a morphism $f:Y\to B$, with these properties. The maps $(t_{s(c)})_{c\in G/\Gamma}$ exhibit $Y$ as the coproduct of copies of $W$ in schemes; they are open immersions with pairwise disjoint clopen images covering $Y$. If $p_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is its structure map, then
$$t_{g\gamma}=t_g\circ d_\gamma,\qquad p_Y\circ t_g=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi(g)^{-1})\circ p,\qquad a_h\circ t_g=t_{hg},\qquad f\circ t_g=q.$$
Thus $Y$ realizes the contracted product with relation $(g\gamma,w)\sim(g,d_\gamma w)$; different choices of representatives give isomorphic objects preserving all these maps. The action is semilinear,
$$p_Y\circ a_h=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi(h)^{-1})\circ p_Y,$$
and $f$ is a $G$-invariant $e$-morphism. For every scheme $T$ with a morphism $T\to B$, the base change $Y_T=Y\times_B T$ is the coproduct of the copies of $W_T=W\times_B T$ via the base changes of $t_{s(c)}$. If the underlying points of $W_T$ form a nonempty single $\Gamma$-orbit, then the underlying points of $Y_T$ form a nonempty single $G$-orbit. No normality or finiteness of $K/e$, no finite-type hypothesis on $W$ or $B$, and no quotient-existence assumption on $W$ are required. Fields, schemes, spectrum, fibre product, open immersions and coproducts use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-open-immersion], and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

proof.text: Put $C=G/\Gamma$ and write $s_c=s(c)$. Every $g\in G$ has a unique expression $g=s_c\eta(g)$, where $c=g\Gamma$ and $\eta(g)=s_c^{-1}g\in\Gamma$. Thus $\eta(g\gamma)=\eta(g)\gamma$. Put $S_g=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi(g)^{-1})$. Contravariant functoriality of spectrum gives $S_{gh}=S_g\circ S_h$ and $S_1=1$: indeed $\pi(gh)^{-1}=\pi(h)^{-1}\circ\pi(g)^{-1}$. Every $S_g$ is over $\operatorname{Spec}e$ because $\pi(g)$ fixes $e$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to form $Y=\coprod_{c\in C}W$, with coprojections $j_c$. Define $p_Y$ by $p_Yj_c=S_{s_c}p$ and $t_g=j_{g\Gamma}d_{\eta(g)}$. The coproduct universal property gives $p_Y$, and its open-immersion and disjoint-cover clauses give all the required assertions about the maps $t_{s_c}=j_c$. The action law of $d$ gives $t_{g\gamma}=j_{g\Gamma}d_{\eta(g)\gamma}=t_gd_\gamma$. Also $p_Yt_g=S_{s_c}p d_{\eta(g)}=S_{s_c}S_{\eta(g)}p=S_gp$.

proof.text: For each $h\in G$ define $a_h$ uniquely by $a_hj_c=t_{hs_c}$. Then for $g=s_c\eta$, $a_ht_g=t_{hs_c}d_\eta=t_{hg}$. Consequently $a_1j_c=j_c$ and $a_ha_kj_c=t_{hks_c}=a_{hk}j_c$; coproduct uniqueness proves $a_1=1$ and $a_ha_k=a_{hk}$. In particular $a_{h^{-1}}$ is the inverse of $a_h$. On each coprojection, $p_Ya_hj_c=S_{hs_c}p=S_hS_{s_c}p=S_hp_Yj_c$. Uniqueness proves $p_Ya_h=S_hp_Y$.

proof.text: Define $f$ uniquely by $fj_c=q$. For $g=s_c\eta$, invariance of $q$ gives $ft_g=q d_\eta=q$; hence $fa_hj_c=ft_{hs_c}=q=fj_c$, so $fa_h=f$. Let $b:B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ and $r:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ be the structure maps. On $j_c$, $b f j_c=bq=rp=rS_{s_c}p=rp_Yj_c$, and therefore $bf=rp_Y$. Thus $f$ is an $e$-morphism and each $a_h$ is an $e$-automorphism.

proof.text: The relation is realized with its mapping property: if maps $b_g:W\to Z$ to any scheme satisfy $b_{g\gamma}=b_gd_\gamma$, the unique map $b:Y\to Z$ with $bj_c=b_{s_c}$ satisfies $bt_g=b_{s_c}d_{\eta(g)}=b_g$. Conversely a map out of $Y$ gives such a family. For another representative system, write its construction as $(Y',t'_g)$. The unique map $\phi:Y\to Y'$ with $\phi j_c=t'_{s_c}$ satisfies $\phi t_g=t'_g$. Construct the reverse map using the other representatives. Their composites fix every coprojection, hence are identities. The identities already proved on all $t_g$ imply that $\phi$ preserves the scalar map, the invariant map and the action.

proof.text: Let $T\to B$ be arbitrary, and put $W_T=W\times_BT$, with projections $u:W_T\to W$ and $\tau:W_T\to T$. Define the codiagonal $r_Y:Y\to W$ by $r_Yj_c=1_W$. Coproduct uniqueness gives $f=q r_Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-base-change] with $U=W$, $V=W_T$, its morphism $v=u$, and $E=C$. It identifies $\coprod_C W_T$ with $W_T\times_WY$. Write $\alpha,\beta$ for the projections of $W_T\times_WY$ to $W_T,Y$. The morphism to $Y\times_BT$ has components $(\beta,\tau\alpha)$; these are compatible since $f\beta=q r_Y\beta=q u\alpha$. Conversely the projections $(y,t)$ of $Y\times_BT$ give $(r_Yy,t)$ into $W_T$, since $q r_Yy=fy=t|_B$, and then $((r_Yy,t),y)$ into $W_T\times_WY$. Both composites are identities by equality of their projections. On the $c$-th summand these formulas give $j_c\times_B1_T$. This proves the asserted base-change coproduct.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, contracted products and diagram (2.b); explicit left-action coset construction. Scheme coproduct input: Stacks Tags 01JB (lemma-glue) and 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes).

proof.text: Since $qd_\gamma=q$ and $fa_h=f$, the maps $d_\gamma\times_B1_T$ and $a_h\times_B1_T$ exist and satisfy the action laws by fibre-product uniqueness. The identity $a_ht_g=t_{hg}$ remains true after base change. Write the base-changed maps as $t_{g,T}$. The coproduct in the preceding step implies every underlying point of $Y_T$ is $t_{s_c,T}(w)$ for a point $w$ of $W_T$. If $W_T$ is nonempty and transitive, two points are $t_{s_c,T}(w)$ and $t_{s_b,T}(w\prime)$ with $w\prime=d_{\gamma,T}(w)$ for some $\gamma\in\Gamma$. The element $h=s_b\gamma s_c^{-1}$ carries the first to $t_{s_b\gamma,T}(w)=t_{s_b,T}(w\prime)$, the second. The image under $t_{1,T}$ of any point of $W_T$ proves nonemptiness. No condition on $K/e$ beyond the stated field action, and no finiteness or quotient-existence property of schemes, was used.
